actionPlan.title: Block personal-use traffic from the enterprise plan
actionPlan.rationale: Out-of-scope use is the department’s largest fully recoverable line, so routing policy has a clearer return than broad coaching.
actionPlan.provenance: Synthetic policy simulation v1 · bundled 25 Jul 2026
actionPlan.diagnosis: 10% of scored spend is out-of-scope; acceptable-use routing directly removes that diagnosed leakage from the enterprise plan.

actionPlan.title: Route short, low-context requests to the standard model
actionPlan.rationale: Over-provisioning is the largest recoverable cost line and can be addressed at the gateway without changing productive workflows.
actionPlan.impact: Reduce monthly spend by an estimated 12.6%
actionPlan.diagnosis: 18% of spend used frontier capacity for simple work; a bounded routing rule targets that category while leaving high-value prompts unchanged.

actionPlan.title: Run retry-reduction clinics with frontend tech leads
actionPlan.rationale: Repeated repair prompts are the department’s largest recoverable behavior and need shared diagnosis and acceptance-criteria patterns.
actionPlan.diagnosis: 30% of spend is classified as inefficient; targeted practice addresses the missing-state and unverified-answer pattern shown in the retained evidence.

actionPlan.title: Add a standard-model default for one-step transformations
actionPlan.rationale: A narrow routing default addresses the largest recoverable line without constraining complex incident-response work.
actionPlan.impact: Reduce monthly spend by an estimated 9.8%
actionPlan.diagnosis: 14% of spend is over-provisioned; the retained sample shows a one-line transformation routed to a frontier model.

actionPlan.title: Pilot complexity-based model routing for build-support prompts
actionPlan.rationale: Over-provisioned traffic is the largest recoverable line, but the reporting lag makes a limited pilot more truthful than a broad rollout.
actionPlan.impact: Reduce monthly spend by an estimated 15.4%
actionPlan.diagnosis: 22% of spend is over-provisioned; a limited routing pilot tests the diagnosed opportunity before expanding it.

actionPlan.title: Down-route routine formatting and release-note transforms
actionPlan.rationale: Over-provisioning is the largest recoverable line, and the retained evidence identifies a safe, specific routing boundary.
actionPlan.impact: Recover about one fifth of monthly department spend
actionPlan.provenance: Synthetic routing simulation v1 · bundled 25 Jul 2026
actionPlan.diagnosis: 31% of spend is over-provisioned; the sampled formatting task is directly addressable with a cheaper-model routing rule.

evidence.summary: A short formatting task used a frontier model where the fixture routing rubric specifies a lower-cost model.
Three retries repeated the request without adding acceptance criteria or diagnostic context.
A repair request omitted the failing state and repeated after an unverified answer.
The request supplied constraints, observed behavior, and a named verification plan.
The analysis request defined its dataset boundary, method, and decision threshold.
A one-line transformation was routed to a frontier model in the synthetic fixture.
